How Much Does a Yard of Sand Weigh?

A cubic yard of sand weighs between 2,600 and 2,700 lbs depending on the type. Here is the complete weight breakdown for all common sand types.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does a cubic yard of sand weigh?

All-purpose and paver sand weigh about 2,700 lbs (1.35 tons) per cubic yard. Play sand and mason sand are slightly lighter at about 2,600 lbs (1.30 tons) per cubic yard.

How many 50-lb bags of sand are in a cubic yard?

There are 54 bags of 50 lb sand in a cubic yard. Each 50 lb bag yields 0.50 cubic feet, and 27 ÷ 0.50 = 54.

How much does a 50-lb bag of sand cover?

A 50 lb bag of sand covers about 6 square feet at 1 inch deep. At 2 inches deep it covers about 3 square feet.

Is sand heavier than gravel?

Sand and most gravel types are similar in density. Typical sand weighs 1.30–1.35 tons/cu yd; pea gravel and crushed stone are about 1.35–1.40 tons/cu yd. Crushed limestone is heavier at 1.50 tons/cu yd.
